property_summary: A forward call should not modify the storage state of the calling contract C

A call to forward always succeeds regardless of callee and data, because low-level call reverts only on failure but does not modify C's storage, whereas delegatecall can fail or corrupt C's state causing subsequent reverts.
A forward call must never revert
A forward call must never revert.
A forward call must never revert.
After any call to forward, the C contract's owner remains unchanged because the external call is executed in a separate context; the bug allows the callee to overwrite C's owner via delegatecall.
After forward is called, the caller of the test remains the same, but the bug allows the callee to change the caller of the test.
After any invocation of forward, owner must remain unchanged because the external call executes in a separate context; the bug allows the callee to change owner via delegatecall.

After any call to forward, address(this) balance of a fresh test helper remains zero because the reference performs a call in the helper's context; the bug performs a delegatecall running in C's context, so the helper receives no ETH and cannot forward it, thus address(this) balance stays zero in the bug.
A failed external call must cause the entire forward transaction to revert.
